recommendation: Keep the audit commit. If current build-warning severity policy needs to change, review current QA output and make any implementation in the active publishing/Kindling tooling rather than in FHIR core spec source or suppression lists for FHIR-8650.
issue_request: FHIR-8650 is Published/Persuasive for FHIR-core/FHIR-Tools-Core. It asked, following an FMG decision, that most build-result WARNINGs be downgraded to INFORMATION, leaving only the search-parameter illegal-type warning and the CodeableConcept/Coding-without-binding warning as true warnings.
initial_application: The Jira application record is Grahame Grieve's comment 'svn revision 6893'. The current Git history has no FHIR-8650-tagged commit and does not contain the old SVN revision, so the historical application cannot be replayed as a current core-source patch.
additional_context: The current FHIR checkout delegates publication/QA to tools/java/org.hl7.fhir.tools.core.jar from build.xml, and that Java tooling is not tracked in this spec checkout. The local Kindling tooling checkout shows ResourceValidator.hint() emits IssueSeverity.INFORMATION and the CodeableConcept/Coding binding diagnostic uses hint(). Later warning suppression inputs in the spec history reflect separate current QA exceptions and should not be mass-edited for this old tooling issue.
reconciliation: Published an empty external-repo audit commit on the combined branch. No FHIR core source files were changed because the actionable behavior is build-tool severity logic outside this checkout, and the available tooling source already treats the named binding diagnostic as informational.
